S9.label: section 9 of the Veldra Personal Data Act 2016

S14.label: section 14 of the Veldra Personal Data Act 2016

S21.label: section 21 of the Veldra Personal Data Act 2016

attrs.facts: A former politician asked a news site to delete a 2009 archive article about a dropped criminal charge.
A mobile operator sold location histories of customers to advertisers without asking them.
A bank read the work e-mails of a clerk who had signed a consent form in her employment contract.
A software firm tracked keystrokes of employees who had ticked a consent box on their first day.
A patient asked a private clinic to erase records of a mental health stay from twelve years earlier.
An insurer built risk profiles from customers' shopping data and claimed customers had agreed in the policy terms.

L-01.title_hint: Erasure of old personal records after Rusk v. Oberline Health
L-01.issue: When must an old record about a person be erased under section 14, and does the public interest in archives outweigh it?
L-01.thesis: Rusk narrows Marrin: the archive exception covers press archives only, not private records.

L-02.title_hint: Legitimate interest as a basis for profiling after Halden Mobile
L-02.issue: Can a company rely on its legitimate interest under section 21 to build profiles of customers?
L-02.thesis: Halden sets a strict test that lower courts apply unevenly; consent clauses in standard terms do not fill the gap.

L-03.title_hint: Employee consent to monitoring: Ostra Bank and Pell in conflict
L-03.issue: Is an employee's consent under section 9 a valid basis for monitoring at work?
L-03.thesis: The courts disagree; Pell is the better view because consent at work is rarely free.
